summary: Sandy Neck Light at Barnstable Harbor: an 1826 or 1827 light, the 1857 brick tower, given up in 1931 or 1932, and relit by volunteers in 2007. Privately owned and closed.

access.note: Privately owned; grounds, dwelling and tower closed.

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends describes a wooden tower in 1826 and the present forty-eight-foot brick tower of 1857; the USLHS record gives the tower established year as 1857.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends gives 1 October 1826 as the date the light went into service; the USLHS record and the Barnstable Harbor history give 1827 as the year the station was established. Both are reported; neither is resolved.
The USLHS record gives 1931; LighthouseFriends says the government surplused the lighthouse in 1932, and its last keeper, Simeon A. Orne, is on the roster to 1932. Both are reported.
LighthouseFriends says James Baxter took over in 1844; the roster carries Henry Baxter to 1846 and lists no James Baxter. Not resolved.

notes_for_editor: (1) Most of the keeper history, the family anecdotes, the 1932-2010 history and the access details come from LighthouseFriends, which quotes logbooks and newspapers it does not reproduce. Nothing was checked in a logbook or in the Cape Cod Times and Lighthouse Digest pieces its references list. All are attributed to it in the text. (2) First lit: LighthouseFriends gives 1 October 1826; the USLHS record and the Barnstable Harbor history give 1827. Both are in the text. (3) Discontinuance: USLHS 1931; LighthouseFriends surplus 1932; Orne on the roster to 1932. Both are in the text. (4) Tower height: LighthouseFriends gives 48 ft for the 1857 brick tower. The USLHS record's tower height is 40 ft and its focal height 47 ft; the record's 16 m for a brick 1826 tower merges the 1826 wooden light with the 1857 tower. Not resolved; the story gives LighthouseFriends' height only. (5) The USLHS record gives the original optic as a fifth-order Fresnel lens and the current one as a LED; the LighthouseFriends text read does not name the original order, so the story gives none. (6) Henry Baxter and the 1844 James Baxter claim: unresolved; the roster and LighthouseFriends disagree. (7) Chronicling America: 'Sandy Neck' with 'lighthouse', Massachusetts, 1900-1935, returned no hits. The local Bulletin text for 1929-1939 has no Sandy Neck discontinuance notice (the 'Sandy Neck' grep found only Wings Neck and unrelated items). (8) NRHP: the Sandy Neck Cultural Resources District nomination (NRHP 87000305, listed 1987) is marked 'not yet digitized' at NPGallery, so the record's 'contributing property' status is not verified and is not in the story. (9) The 1900 boathouse storm is undated in the Board's report; the story says so. (10) The Bailey link between Sandy Neck and Monomoy Point is on this record's line. (11) The daughter of the keeper quoted in the 1974 interview is not named; the restoration committee chairman is not named. (12) The Barnstable Harbor page was read as a landing page only; its linked full history was not followed. Wikipedia was not used. (13) No photographs were found or proposed. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-22: (a) the 2 December entry is printed in the 1926 Bulletin without a year, in a list whose other dated entries are December 1925, so the story says 1925 is inferred and the event year is 1925; the Bulletin index's 'assists vessel 119, 256' gives Bulletin page numbers, not vessel numbers, so the story does not read them as vessels; (b) the Hinckley family is no longer named in the story (private owners; the record names them only as owners); (c) the Ellis names are kept as the source gives them, 1942 and earlier; (d) 'the harbor was hard on the light from the start' and the 'family feared' phrasing were removed as unsourced atmosphere; (e) 'The land approach runs over private property' had no source and was replaced by LighthouseFriends' access statement.
